transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you saw a problem that wasn't yours to fix, and you fixed it anyway.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: Our data pipeline was dropping records silently. I noticed it debugging something else. I wrote a reconciliation script, identified 4,000 dropped records, backfilled them, and added a daily row-count alert. The data team was surprised — they hadn't known.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate on a technical decision.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: My lead wanted rate limiting in each service. I thought shared middleware was cleaner. We spent an hour whiteboarding. I acknowledged his coupling concern. We went with middleware but per-service config override.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you were wrong about something technical.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I was convinced distributed transactions were right until a colleague showed me Pat Helland's talk. I rebuilt around event sourcing and the result was much simpler.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: What's a weakness you've had to actively work on?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I have a tendency to take over problems when I see a faster path. I've had to learn to hold back and let teammates work through things at their own pace, even when it's slower.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you had to push back on a direction you disagreed with.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: My manager wanted to ship without instrumentation. I pushed back in a 1:1, walked through risks, and we agreed on basic event logging first and full analytics next sprint.
